Turkey Cooking Time Calculator

At 325 °F, a 12 to 14 lb unstuffed turkey takes 3 to 3¾ hours; stuffed, 3½ to 4 hours. It’s done at 165 °F in the thickest part of the thigh. Rest it 20 minutes before carving.

USDA turkey roasting times at 325 °F

Fresh or thawed whole turkey, oven at 325 °F
WeightUnstuffedStuffed
8 to 12 lb2¾ to 3 hours3 to 3½ hours
12 to 14 lb3 to 3¾ hours3½ to 4 hours
14 to 18 lb3¾ to 4¼ hours4 to 4¼ hours
18 to 20 lb4¼ to 4½ hours4¼ to 4¾ hours
20 to 24 lb4½ to 5 hours4¾ to 5¼ hours

Source: USDA roasting timetable for fresh or thawed turkey at 325 °F, as published by University of Illinois Extension. Times are approximate; the thermometer decides.

Thawing in the refrigerator

Allow about 1 day for every 4 pounds
TurkeyDays in the fridge
8 lb2 days
12 lb3 days
16 lb4 days
20 lb5 days
24 lb6 days

Thaw in the refrigerator, breast side up, in its wrapper on a tray. Never thaw a turkey on the counter: the outside sits at room temperature long enough for bacteria to grow while the middle is still frozen.

How it works

Enter the weight and whether it’s stuffed, and the calculator looks up the USDA time range for that weight at 325 °F. Add your serving time and it tells you when the turkey needs to go in: the longer end of the range plus the 20-minute rest. The USDA times are for 325 °F; don’t roast a turkey any lower than that. It all runs in your browser. Nothing you type is sent anywhere or saved.

Done means 165 °F

Check the innermost part of the thigh, the wing and the thickest part of the breast. If it’s stuffed, the center of the stuffing has to reach 165 °F too. Then let it rest 20 minutes before carving, so the juices settle back into the meat.

About stuffing

Stuff the turkey just before it goes in the oven, never the night before, and stuff it loosely. The USDA recommends baking the stuffing in a separate dish, which cooks more evenly and takes time off the roast.

Ways to use it

  • Thanksgiving. Work back from dinner time to when it goes in the oven, and from that to when it comes out of the freezer.
  • Christmas. Same math, a month later.
  • Meal prep. A whole turkey is a week of sandwiches and soup.

Questions

How long per pound?

It isn’t a straight per-pound number, because big birds cook faster per pound than small ones. The USDA chart gives ranges by weight: 2¾ to 3 hours for 8 to 12 lb, up to 4½ to 5 hours for 20 to 24 lb, unstuffed at 325 °F.

Stuffed or unstuffed?

Unstuffed is faster and cooks more evenly, which is why the USDA suggests baking stuffing in a separate dish. A stuffed turkey takes about 15 to 30 minutes longer, and the stuffing must reach 165 °F.

What temperature is done?

165 °F in the innermost part of the thigh, the wing and the thickest part of the breast, measured with a food thermometer. For a stuffed turkey, the center of the stuffing must reach 165 °F too.

How long do I rest it?

20 minutes before carving. The temperature keeps rising a little and the juices settle, so the meat stays moist when you slice it.

How many days to thaw?

About 1 day in the refrigerator for every 4 pounds, so a 12 lb turkey needs 3 days and a 20 lb turkey needs 5. Never thaw it on the counter.
